name: GetRender
tagline: Turns architectural sketches, CAD views and massing models into photorealistic renders with AI.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is image-to-image conditioned on structure: take a line drawing or clay render, keep the geometry, hallucinate materials, light and landscaping. That is a solved pattern with a depth or canny ControlNet on top of an open base model, and an agent can wire the whole pipeline plus a drop-zone UI in a weekend. What you will not match quickly is the tuning: hosted architectural renderers have been fed a lot of interior and exterior imagery and their prompt presets quietly encode what a decent render looks like, so your first outputs will have melted window mullions and furniture that defies gravity. You also inherit the GPU problem, either a 16GB+ card sitting idle or a hosted inference bill. Good enough for your own concept boards, not good enough to hand a client without a long afternoon of prompt and strength tuning.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop a sketch or SketchUp screenshot, pick an exterior or interior preset, and get structure-preserving photoreal variants back from a ControlNet pipeline.
requirements: An NVIDIA GPU with 16GB+ VRAM, or a hosted inference API key in .env
Python 3.11 and roughly 20GB of disk for model weights
A Hugging Face token for gated base model weights
Patience for tuning ControlNet strength per drawing style
whatYouLose: Models tuned specifically on architectural and interior imagery, so fewer geometry artifacts out of the box
Curated style presets that already know what "Scandinavian interior, overcast afternoon" should look like
Built-in upscaling to print or presentation resolution without a second pipeline
Fast turnaround from a phone or a laptop with no GPU
Client-facing sharing, versioning and anything resembling a project folder
moatNotes: The fine-tune and the preset library are the product. The base diffusion tech is commodity and has been for a while.
whyPeopleStillPay: Architects and interior designers are paying to skip a GPU, a weights directory and an evening of guessing at conditioning strength. The value is that a bad render is worthless, and tuned models plus hand-tested presets raise the floor so the fifth output is usable instead of the fiftieth. A practice billing by the hour will not self-host this, and the people who would enjoy self-hosting it were never the customer.
notes: The pipeline is a weekend, the taste baked into the presets is not. Budget your time for prompt tuning, not for code.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user web app called "renderbench" that turns architectural sketches and clay renders into photorealistic images while preserving geometry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, Uvicorn.
- Hugging Face diffusers for inference: SDXL base plus a depth ControlNet, with canny ControlNet as a selectable second mode.
- Depth maps generated locally with Depth-Anything-V2 small.
- Frontend: one server-rendered HTML page with vanilla JS and plain CSS. No React, no build step.
- SQLite via sqlite3 for job history. Files on disk under ./data.

In scope:
- Drag-and-drop upload of PNG or JPG (sketch, CAD export, SketchUp screenshot).
- Mode selector: exterior or interior. Each mode is a hardcoded prompt preset in presets.py with positive prompt, negative prompt, ControlNet conditioning scale and a sensible step count. Keep presets editable in one file.
- Free-text prompt box appended to the preset prompt.
- Sliders for conditioning scale (0.3 to 1.2) and denoise strength, with the preset value as default.
- Generate 4 variants per run with different seeds, show them in a grid, click to open full size.
- Job history page listing past runs with thumbnail, prompt, seed and settings, so a good result is reproducible.
- Optional Real-ESRGAN 2x upscale button per image.
- If RENDER_API_KEY and RENDER_API_URL are set in .env, route generation to that hosted endpoint instead of local weights. Otherwise run locally. Detect CUDA and fail loudly with a readable message if there is no GPU and no API key.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, auth, cloud storage, telemetry, analytics, payment, sharing links, mobile app, 3D file parsing of any kind (images in, images out).

Deliverables: requirements.txt, .env.example with HF_TOKEN, RENDER_API_KEY, RENDER_API_URL, a README with exact setup commands, approximate weight download size and first-run time, and three sample presets. Secrets only from .env, never hardcoded. Include a short README section on tuning conditioning scale per drawing style, because defaults will be wrong for hand sketches.
